fact_text: A third-country national relocating to Thailand to work must hold a Non-Immigrant Visa category "B" (Business Visa), applied for at a Royal Thai Embassy/Consulate before entry; it is issued to those who wish to enter the Kingdom to work or conduct business.
evidence_quote: is issued to applicants who wish to enter the Kingdom to work or to conduct business

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed a long-stay or tourist entry lets an employee start work. Actually working requires the specific Non-Immigrant "B" visa, normally obtained from a Thai embassy abroad before arrival. Action: secure the Non-B visa before the employee relocates.

fact_text: Holding the Non-Immigrant "B" visa is not enough to work: the visa holder wishing to work in Thailand must be granted a work permit before starting work.
evidence_quote: must be granted a work permit before starting work

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed the "work visa" (Non-B) by itself authorises employment. Actually the visa and the work permit are two separate documents and no work may begin until the work permit is issued. Action: do not let the employee start duties before the work permit is granted.

fact_text: The work authorisation is employer-driven and employer-specific: to obtain the Ministry of Labour approval needed for the Non-B visa, the applicant's prospective employer in Thailand must submit Form WP3 and the hiring company's corporate documents to the Department of Employment.
evidence_quote: the applicant's prospective employer in Thailand is required to submit Form WP3 at the Office of Foreign Workers Administration, Department of Employment, Ministry of Labour

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed the employee arranges their own work rights. Actually the specific hiring employer must initiate them (Form WP3) and file the company's corporate documents, so the authorisation is tied to that employer. Action: have the Thai employer, not the employee, start the WP3 process.

entity_title: No work on temporary stay without permission
fact_text: Under the Immigration Act, an alien permitted to stay temporarily (including on a tourist visa or visa exemption) may not engage in an occupation or employment except with permission from the Director-General or the competent official.
evidence_quote: except with permission from the Director-General or the competent official

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed a little work is fine while on a tourist/visa-exempt entry. Actually the Immigration Act bars any employment during a temporary stay unless specifically permitted (i.e. a work permit); a tourist entry grants no such permission. Action: never begin work on a tourist or visa-exempt entry.

entity_title: Re-entry permit preserves stay when leaving
fact_text: Leaving Thailand cancels a temporary stay permission unless a re-entry permit was obtained first: if the alien leaves the Kingdom it shall be deemed that the temporary stay permission is terminated, so a re-entry permit must be applied for before departure to keep the visa valid.
evidence_quote: it shall be deemed that the temporary stay permission is terminated

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed a valid multi-entry-looking visa stays valid through any trip abroad. Actually a single-entry Non-B stay permission is terminated the moment the holder leaves unless a re-entry permit was granted beforehand. Action: buy a re-entry permit before any trip out of Thailand.

fact_text: A foreigner staying in Thailand longer than 90 days must notify the Immigration authorities in writing of their current address, repeated at every 90-day interval, separately from any visa or work-permit renewal.
evidence_quote: Staying in the Kingdom longer than ninety days, an alien shall notify the competent official at the Immigration Division, of his or her residence, in writing, without delay

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed once your visa is sorted there is nothing further to file. Actually every long-stay foreigner must lodge a 90-day address report each 90 days, and lateness carries a fine. Action: diarise the recurring 90-day report from the date of entry/last report.

fact_text: For eligible skilled professionals, executives and investors in targeted industries, the SMART Visa is an alternative to the Non-B + work-permit route: Smart Visa holders are granted a maximum 4-year permission to stay and an exemption from the work permit requirement.
evidence_quote: Smart Visa holders will be granted maximum 4-year permission to stay, exemption from the work permit requirement and entitled to additional privileges

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed every foreign professional must run the Non-B visa plus annual work-permit cycle. Actually qualifying talent in BOI targeted industries can use the SMART Visa, which grants up to 4 years and waives the work permit. Action: check SMART Visa eligibility before defaulting to Non-B + work permit.

fact_text: A relocating employee becomes a Thai tax resident once they reside in Thailand for periods aggregating more than 180 days in a calendar (tax) year.
evidence_quote: means any person residing in Thailand for a period or periods aggregating more than 180 days in any tax (calendar) year

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed tax residency follows the visa or the employment contract. Actually it is a day-count: more than 180 days in the calendar year makes you a Thai tax resident, which widens what income Thailand can tax. Action: track days present and plan the arrival month accordingly.

fact_text: A Thai tax resident is liable to tax not only on Thai-source income but also on the portion of foreign-source income that is brought into Thailand.
evidence_quote: as well as on the portion of income from foreign sources that is brought into Thailand

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed salary or savings paid into a foreign account are outside Thai tax. Actually a Thai tax resident is taxed on foreign-source income remitted into Thailand, and the Revenue Department has recently tightened how remittances are treated. Action: confirm current remittance treatment with the Revenue Department before transferring foreign funds in.

entity_title: Employer must enrol staff in Social Security
fact_text: An employer of insured employees (which includes foreign employees working under the Social Security Act) must file employer and insured registration with the Social Security Office within 30 days of the employee becoming an insured person.
evidence_quote: shall file an employer registration form and insured registration form to the Office within thirty days

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed Social Security is only for Thai nationals or is optional if the company provides private insurance. Actually employers must enrol qualifying employees (foreigners included) within 30 days, on top of any private cover. Action: confirm the employee is registered with the SSO within 30 days of hire.

entity_title: Social Security contributions deducted from pay
fact_text: Social Security is contributory: the Government, the employer and the insured person each remit contributions to the Fund, and the employer deducts the employee's share from wages and remits it.
evidence_quote: The Government, an employer and an insured person under section 33 shall each equally remit contributions to the Fund

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed take-home pay equals gross salary or that only the employer pays. Actually the employee's Social Security contribution is deducted from wages each pay period alongside the employer and government shares. Action: expect a Social Security deduction on the employee's Thai payslip.

fact_text: Under the SMART "O" category, the legal dependants (spouse and children) of a main SMART Visa holder are permitted to live and work in Thailand equivalent to the SMART Visa holder.
evidence_quote: the legal dependents spouse and children of the main Smart Visa holders to live and work in Thailand equivalent to Smart Visa holders

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed an accompanying spouse on a dependant visa cannot work without their own employer-sponsored work permit. Actually SMART "O" dependants of a SMART Visa holder may live and work in Thailand. Action: if using SMART Visa, check SMART "O" for a working spouse.
